clue.text: Disappear without the right coat

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the vanishing word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to disappear is to vanish
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone vanishes before they have put on the correct coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: R goes inside VANISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is a glossy protective layer brushed onto wood, a coat in the decorator's sense.

clue.text: Leaders out West will get a taste

parts.note: the van is the vanguard, those at the front

indicators.note: out says the letter for West is removed from will

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Frontier chiefs in the Wild West will try a flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out West' reads as the American frontier, but 'out' removes W from WILL, leaving ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is a flavouring from orchid pods, so it is a flavour or taste.

clue.text: Ordering a realignment of the Mexican border

indicators.note: a realignment of the words means their letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A government orders the boundary with Mexico to be redrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river forms much of the frontier between the USA and Mexico.

clue.text: Bone discovered in Troy

definitions.meaning: the broad upper bone of the pelvis
the Latin name of the ancient city besieged by the Greeks

explanation.surface: Archaeologists unearth a bone at the site of ancient Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilium is the large hip bone, and Ilium was the classical name of the city of Priam.

clue.text: When drinks are cheap, dwarf and nymph forgoing one

parts.note: Happy is one of the Seven Dwarfs in the Snow White tale

indicators.note: forgoing means going without, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful maiden of the Islamic paradise
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dwarf and a nymph give up a drink each when the prices drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgoing one' removes I from HOURI, leaving HOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy hour is the period when a bar sells drinks at reduced prices.

clue.text: Druggist initially mixing powder and a little water

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word Druggist
mixing tells us the letters of powder are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemist starts blending a powder with a small amount of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little water' sounds like an ingredient in the druggist's mixture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A single bead of moisture formed on grass at dawn is a tiny quantity of water.

clue.text: Try to stop animals going outside the forest's boundary

indicators.note: going outside means the animals wrap around the other piece

parts.note: deer are animals of the forest

indicators.note: boundary picks the edge letter of forest, here its last

explanation.surface: Someone tries to keep wild animals from straying past the forest's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundary' takes the final letter of 'forest's', T, which goes inside DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage or prevent someone from acting.

clue.text: Fanciful claim — wish to make it?

indicators.note: to make it asks us to build the answer by rearranging the two words before

explanation.surface: Someone makes an extravagant claim and wishes to make it come true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make it' rearranges CLAIM WISH into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical means playfully quaint or capricious, driven by fancy.

clue.text: Have power but fall, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says a word for fall is replaced by one that is pronounced the same

parts.note: rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A ruler holds power and then is overthrown, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch reigns, that is rules and holds sovereign authority.

clue.text: Display long face at first

indicators.note: at first puts the face piece at the front, ahead of the longing

parts.note: pan is slang for face, as in deadpan
to long is to ache for something

explanation.surface: Someone shows a long face to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long face' reads as a gloomy expression, but the two words work separately, and 'at first' puts the face word in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant style, a confident display.

clue.text: I complain about girl. .

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole phrase I plus the complaint is read backwards

parts.note: to complain is to moan

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a young woman, and the sentence trails into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole of I + MOAN round, giving NAOMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: … with a name that's aristocratic

parts.note: the girl carried over by the ellipsis from 9-across is given here a fuller female first name, and name itself is abbreviated to N
the girl carried over by the ellipsis from 9-across is given here a fuller female first name, and name itself is abbreviated to N

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the girl turns out to have a posh name.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'girl' over from 9-across: here the girl is PATRICIA, followed by N for 'name'.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrician was a member of the Roman nobility, so the word means noble or upper-class.

clue.text: He is coached in the City for his show

definitions.text: He is coached in the City for his show

parts.words: He is coached in the City for his show
parts.note: describes the civic head of the City of London riding in a gilded state coach in his annual procession through the streets

explanation.surface: Someone is driven through the City in a carriage for a public parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coached' looks like training, but it means carried in a coach. The City is the City of London, whose newly chosen civic head rides in a golden coach in the Show held each November.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of this office is the figure who rides in the gold coach at the Show in the City of London.

clue.text: Original Spitfire operational, I see — by the sound of it, doing 743 mph

indicators.note: Original asks for the opening letter of the word Spitfire

parts.note: something operational is switched on

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word see is replaced by the letter that is pronounced the same way

parts.note: see is pronounced like the letter C

explanation.surface: A wartime fighter plane is up and running and appears to be flying at enormous speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 743 mph is roughly the speed of sound at sea level, so the definition is a figure rather than a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at about 743 mph means travelling at the speed of sound waves through air.

clue.text: Get some small number admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: some can mean any, as in 'have you got any?'
No. is the short form of number, hence a small version of the word

explanation.surface: Obtain a little figure that has been allowed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is the definition in its sense of irritate, as in 'it really gets me'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone, informally, is to irritate or bother them.

clue.text: Contemptible person opposed to trade unions in US

definitions.text: opposed to trade unions in US
definitions.meaning: in American usage, describing contracts or employers that bar union membership

explanation.surface: A despicable figure in America is against organised labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-dog is a cur or coward, and a yellow-dog contract in the US forbade workers from joining a union.

clue.text: Thing I have detached

parts.note: an object is a thing
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A possession of mine is no longer attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Objective views are impartial, unaffected by personal feeling, hence detached.

clue.text: Aircraft has about right power for high winds

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft

indicators.note: about means round, so the power word wraps the letter for right

parts.note: steam is a source of power, as in steam engines

explanation.surface: A plane carries roughly the correct thrust for strong winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about right' reads as 'approximately correct'; in fact 'about' puts R inside STEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet stream is a band of very fast winds high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: I start to nurse Tommy behind closed doors

indicators.note: start to asks for the opening letter of the word nurse

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is the nickname for a British private soldier

explanation.surface: A nurse starts work on a soldier in seclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is the traditional nickname for a British army private.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in private is done secretly, away from the public.

clue.text: The Pied Piper might become suspicious

definitions.meaning: the legendary piper of Hamelin who lured away the town's rodents might detect one by its odour
to sense that something is wrong or underhand

explanation.surface: The legendary piper of Hamelin starts to have doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sensing trickery, and literally a rodent-catcher might catch a whiff of his quarry.

clue.text: Fears it may break, though it's fine, with no sign of breaking

definitions.text: fine, with no sign of breaking

indicators.note: may break says the letters of fears it are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A forecaster fears the weather will turn although it is fine and settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may break' looks like the weather breaking, but it rearranges FEARS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair is the barometer reading for settled weather, sunny with no change expected.

clue.text: Two trainees about to copy part of a garment

indicators.note: about means round, so the two learner letters stand either side of the other piece

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate, so two of them give LL
to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: A pair of apprentices are about to replicate a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to'; split it, 'about' is the container and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded-back front flap of a jacket or coat, one section of the garment.

clue.text: The way the wind blows in the islands

definitions.text: The way the wind blows in the islands

parts.words: The way the wind blows in the islands
parts.note: the direction downwind, and also the name of a Caribbean island chain

explanation.surface: Someone notes which direction the breeze takes in a group of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the downwind direction, and the Leeward Islands are a Caribbean chain.

clue.text: Soldiers show disapproval of anathema .

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: Troops jeer at something they detest.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the UK's part-time military reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something utterly detested or forbidden, like a subject banned in polite company.

clue.text: Fan keeps a pound in the bank

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the fan wraps round the pound

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An enthusiast keeps a pound deposited at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial but is a steep riverbank or cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or headland, such as a high bank by a river.

clue.text: … one Bertie abused too

definitions.note: carries over the previous clue's definition: this answer is also something detested

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so the letters of one Bertie are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Following on, a man called Bertie is mistreated as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 21-across: 'too' means 'also anathema'. 'abused' rearranges ONE BERTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate, French for black beast, is likewise a thing loathed, as the previous clue's definition says.

clue.text: Bishop and Dean get together for a drinking session

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
W R Inge, the 'Gloomy Dean' of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A bishop and a dean meet up for a heavy evening's drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean Inge was a famous early-20th-century Dean of St Paul's in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of heavy drinking or excess.

clue.text: King Arthur

definitions.meaning: the title of the Emperor of Ethiopia
Arthur ..., the British television antiques expert

explanation.surface: The legendary British ruler of Camelot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Arthur' reads as the legend, but it splits: the Ethiopian royal title, and Arthur Negus, a much-loved BBC antiques broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus was the title of Ethiopian rulers, and Arthur Negus presented antiques programmes on British TV.

clue.text: Plenty of cake supplied during a ball

indicators.note: supplied during means put into the middle of the other phrase

parts.note: a ball is a dance
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: Lots of pastries were served at a formal dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a great quantity, more than enough.

clue.text: Part of Edinburgh an autonomous state

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of Scotland's capital declares itself a self-governing nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a West African country, which is a nation or state.

clue.text: Runaway's course ending beyond traffic island

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so the other piece follows the island

parts.note: a refuge is a raised island in the road where pedestrians can wait

indicators.note: ending asks for the last letter of the word course

explanation.surface: A fugitive's route ends past a traffic island.
explanation.walkthrough: A traffic island in British usage is a refuge in mid-road for pedestrians crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone who has fled their homeland, hence one who has run away.

clue.text: 22 inch bats around

indicators.note: around means the crazy word wraps round the island

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, mad
inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm

explanation.surface: Bats fly round a short measure of length.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '22' points to 22-down, BLUFF, used as a verb. Inch is Scottish (from Gaelic) for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluff someone is to deceive them, to lead them astray.
